subject: Longitudinal predictors with cross-sectional dependent variable

messages.author: 189d19347ab44a74
messages.subject: Longitudinal predictors with cross-sectional dependent variable
parts:
Hi,

I have data where my predictors were measured on three separate occasions (C1, C2, C3) and my dependent, observed variable  (P) was measured once on a later occasion. What I am interested in is whether variation in the intercepts (i) or the slope (s) of my predictor is predictive of my outcome variable, P. In other words, I do not want to ignore the longitudinal nature of my predictors and just composite them or take the average value. 

My question is whether, this syntax:

model <- 
'
           i =~ 1*C1 + 1*C2 + 1*C3
           s =~ 1*C1 + 2*C2 + 3*C3
           P ~~ i + s
 '
fit <- growth(model, data=data)
summary(fit)

Is this model and is it appropriate: https://www.dropbox.com/s/72efdtpslnk3ljv/growth-model.pdf?dl=0

Alternatively, does anyone have a suggestion of a different model that would allow me to tease apart the effects of the mean level in my predictor and the slope of my predictor that would allow me to quantify their effect on my outcome variable?

Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Longitudinal predictors with cross-sectional dependent variable
parts: is the model that I am linking to in that image on Dropbox the same as the lavaan model syntax I have written?

No, your model (and description) say you want the growth factors to predict P, but your syntax is simply allowing those 3 variables to correlate.  Instead of a double-tilde, use a single tilde.  Also, if you want to interpret the intercept as the mean of C at Time 1, then the first loading on Slope should be 0.
